title: YouTube caption extraction uses the wrong transcript API methods

evidence.quote: except Exception as e: ... return None

reasoning: The implementation calls instance methods named fetch and list. With the declared youtube-transcript-api dependency range used by this project, the available API is get_transcript/list_transcripts, so these calls raise and are swallowed by the broad exception handler. In practice, the caption path is dead and every video without a mocked _get_captions falls through to yt-dlp audio transcription, which is slower, less reliable, and may require local binaries or OpenAI credentials.
reproduction: Call await YouTubeService(settings)._get_captions("dQw4w9WgXcQ") with youtube-transcript-api 0.6.x installed; AttributeError is caught and the method returns None, causing get_transcript to use audio fallback.
recommendation: Use the library API supported by the pinned dependency, such as YouTubeTranscriptApi.get_transcript(video_id, languages=[...]) and YouTubeTranscriptApi.list_transcripts(video_id), or update the dependency and implementation together. Avoid swallowing AttributeError from programmer/API mismatches as if captions were unavailable.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing caption success test patches _get_captions itself, so it never executes the youtube-transcript-api integration code that is broken.
suggestedRegressionTest: Mock youtube_transcript_api.YouTubeTranscriptApi.get_transcript/list_transcripts or run against a fixture-compatible fake object and assert _get_captions returns joined caption text without falling back to audio.
minimumFixScope: app/services/youtube_service.py plus a direct _get_captions unit test.
